chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is disliked for a man, when he returns from his journey, to knock on his family's door at night until morning.

key_terms.يَطْرُقَ: To knock on the door / to visit abruptly
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic ruling indicating preference against an action

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for a husband returning home from travel at night?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on marital etiquette, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against a husband surprising his wife abruptly at night after travel to allow for preparation and comfort. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and emotional consideration within the household, ensuring the spouse is not caught off-guard or unprepared for intimacy.
